anchors: This skill ships no scripts: the type checker and clippy already do the mechanical part, once the lints below are on.
decision: The Rust data-architecture skill is a checklist plus tool recipes and ships no scripts; the language-neutral principles and workflow stay in coding-data-architecture.

evidence.text: plan docs/plans/2026-11-09-data-architecture-skills.md decision 3 (recommended shape, mirrors coding-rust-performance-review); every lint name in the skill accepted by clippy 0.1.95 on a scratch crate, and disallowed_types / disallowed_methods / max-fn-params-bools measured firing from clippy.toml

reopen_if: A recurring Rust data-architecture review step is done by hand that rustc and clippy cannot do, such as counting raw serde_json::Value fields across a workspace.
why: rustc's type checker and clippy's lints (wildcard_enum_match_arm, indexing_slicing, unwrap_used, disallowed_types, disallowed_methods, fn_params_excessive_bools) already flag the patterns mechanically once switched on; a scanner would need a Rust parser and duplicate them.

anchors: Two shapes, a choice to make per type:
decision: For a value someone else defines, the skill presents an open newtype with named constants and an enum with an explicit unknown variant as a per-type choice, not one house rule.

evidence.text: evidence list for plan task 3: open_enum! used 344 times in the VMM, its copilot-instructions require it for round-tripping protocol values; web rule R13 (explicit open variant, num_enum catch_all). RED R2 opus chose rejection and called the choice unsettled.

reopen_if: One shape proves wrong for a class of values in review, for example an Unknown variant that silently drops a field that had to be written back.
why: A large Rust VMM uses open newtypes plus a fallback arm for every guest and hardware value, while much published Rust uses an Unknown(raw) variant or num_enum catch_all; both keep the unknown value, and which fits depends on whether the code must store and write the value back or mostly acts on known values.

anchors: go only on such a wire DTO, never on the domain type
decision: serde alias, default and old fields for an older format go only on its versioned wire DTO, never on the domain type; the generic skill's Core Principle 7 holds the rule and this skill points at it.

evidence.text: checklist-20261109-review-fixes.md item 2 RED/GREEN (opus): RED quoted 'never to make an old payload parse' against 'This is where serde(alias), serde(default) and old fields live'; GREEN placed both attributes on the wire DTO and none on the domain type.

reopen_if: A real format needs an old-format field on the domain type itself, for example because the old value must be written back unchanged.
why: Keeps one rule said once: the Rust text applies the generic boundary case to serde instead of restating a second, contradicting compatibility rule.
